em_skeleton — 2D region op

• Data kinds: region → region

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "em_skeleton", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

Usage

Eckhardt–Maderlechner-style invariant thinning (the same family as HALCON skeleton).

Source: U. Eckhardt, G. Maderlechner, "Invariant Thinning", Int. J. Pattern Recognition and AI 7:1115-1144 (1993). The implementation rules follow M. Couprie "Note on fifteen 2D parallel thinning algorithms": a clean-room implementation of the EM93 definition. Checked against the EM93 reference outputs published in that note: for shape 1 the skeleton's pixel set matches bit for bit (724/724), for shapes 2/3 the pixel counts match the published values (2434 / 3895). tests/test_regions2.py::test_em_skeleton_matches_published_em93_reference. (No direct comparison with an actual HALCON installation has been made, but it matches the reference output of the same published algorithm that HALCON relies on):

interior = pixel whose 4-neighbours are all foreground

simple = (8,4) simple point (1 foreground 8-connected component ∧ 1 adjacent background 4-connected component)

perfect = the neighbour in some 4-direction is interior, and the opposite direction is background

repeat "delete all pixels that are both simple and perfect simultaneously" until a fixed point

Note: if the note's transcription is implemented literally, "count simple using strong (4) connected components only", the parallel deletion removes diagonal bridges simultaneously and breaks the topology (measured on a counterexample). This implementation, with simple taken as the standard (8,4) simple point, matched the reference output bit for bit, which confirms that this is the correct reading of EM93.

Fully parallel, symmetric (commutes with 90-degree rotation/mirroring), topology-preserving and idempotent. Keeps more branches than the Zhang–Suen-family sk_skeleton (measured 1.4-1.5 times the pixel count = consistent with the character of EM in Couprie's comparison table: symmetric, many branches). Post-processing spurs with pruning is also the same practice as HALCON. Knobs a, b are unused.

Border handling: treat everything outside the image as background (0) (measured; tools/impl2/border_probe.py).
